notes: ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE - not legal advice. It shows how a UK policy pack is written for OpsPilot. The sources are real; the numbers are example choices. Have every control reviewed by qualified counsel, then set illustrative to false, before relying on it.

sources.title: UK GDPR Article 5 - principles, including storage limitation (5(1)(e)) and accountability (5(2))
UK GDPR Article 9 - special category personal data
UK GDPR Article 22 - automated individual decision-making
ICO - Guidance on AI and data protection

approvals.note: Supported by the source: people should be able to obtain human review of significant decisions made solely by automated means. Example choices: requiring approval for any automated action touching a system that processes personal data, and the 24-hour deadline with escalation after 4 hours.

riskRules.note: Supported by the source: special category data needs extra protection. Example choice: treating any AI system that uses it as high risk, and requiring human oversight wherever decisions have significant or critical impact (see also Article 22).

recordKeeping.note: Supported by the source: keep personal data no longer than necessary, and be able to demonstrate compliance. Example choice: 6 years (2190 days) for both, a common business-records period; the law does not set this figure.
